title: A Unified Geometric Framework for Developmental Analysis of Spatial Transcriptomic Data
abstract: arXiv:2608.15306v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: High-throughput single-cell and spatial transcriptomic technologies provide high-resolution snapshots of heterogeneous cellular states, but their destructive nature prevents repeated measurements of the same cells over time. Consequently, temporal and spatial dynamics must be inferred from independently sampled, unaligned cell populations, making it challenging to reconstruct developmental trajectories. Optimal transport (OT) offers a geometric framework for aligning cell populations and inferring developmental trajectories, but many existing approaches focus on modeling the evolution of distributions of cells in gene expression space rather than the relational structure encoded by gene expression networks. To address this limitation, we introduce a geometric framework for analyzing the spatiotemporal evolution of gene expression networks through embeddings in Gromov--Wasserstein (GW) space. translated_title: 空间转录组数据发育分析的统一几何框架
translated_abstract: 高通量单细胞和空间转录组技术提供了异质细胞状态的高分辨率快照，但其破坏性特性阻止了对同一细胞随时间的重复测量。因此，必须从独立采样、未对齐的细胞群体中推断时间和空间动态，这使得重建发育轨迹变得具有挑战性。最优传输（OT）为对齐细胞群体和推断发育轨迹提供了几何框架，但许多现有方法侧重于建模基因表达空间中细胞分布的演变，而非基因表达网络编码的关系结构。为解决这一局限性，我们引入了一个几何框架，通过将每个发育阶段表示为Gromov-Wasserstein（GW）空间中的嵌入，来分析基因表达网络的时空演变。
tldr: 本文提出了一个统一几何框架，利用Gromov-Wasserstein空间嵌入分析空间转录组数据中基因表达网络的时空演变，克服了现有方法忽略关系结构的局限。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a unified geometric framework that analyzes spatiotemporal evolution of gene expression networks in spatial transcriptomic data via Gromov-Wasserstein embeddings, overcoming limitations of existing methods that overlook relational structures.
